title: User guide
summary: Read, download and manage profiles; settings and language.
body:
# Using SIMHarbor

SIMHarbor manages removable eUICC cards locally on a jailbroken iPhone. Card operations require the supported CommCenter extension. This Documents section can be read offline.

## Read and manage profiles

- Pull to refresh Profiles to read the EID, profile list and enabled states.
- Tap a profile to enable, disable, rename it or copy its ICCID.
- Enabling switches the removable card's active line and may interrupt cellular service. The app rereads the card to verify the resulting state.
- Only disabled profiles can be deleted. Your operator determines whether they can be downloaded again.

## Download and QR codes

1. Choose Scan QR to use the camera or select an image containing the operator's activation QR code. The camera continuously focuses; tap the QR code to focus and adjust exposure at that point. A yellow box marks the selected point. Move farther away if the image remains blurred. Manual entry is also available.
2. Use `LPA:1$server$activation-token`. Enter a confirmation code if required. An optional IMEI must contain 15 digits.
3. On the first download, allow the app to access the network. HTTPS uses system and GSMA trust without disabling certificate checks.
4. Keep the app in the foreground until download, installation and notification processing finish. Newly downloaded profiles remain disabled.

## Settings and notifications

The information button opens Card info and settings, Notifications and Signal console.

- Card information includes EID, free storage/working memory, firmware, RSP and profile versions.
- Settings include the default SM-DP+, an unauthenticated HTTP CONNECT proxy, APDU MSS and refresh after switching.
- Automatic install, delete and switch notifications have separate settings. Submit notifications individually or in a batch; remove them after successful submission. Remove-only does not notify the operator.
- An entire-card reset checks the EID and requires typing `RESET`. It removes profiles and has not been tested on the existing card.
- App → Language offers Follow system, English and Simplified Chinese. The interface changes immediately; logs remain English.

## Documents and logs

Search Documents by title, summary or article body. Select text to copy examples and offsets, or use Copy to copy an entire article's displayed text. Reading documentation never executes its examples.

Logs shows English raw signaling with copy, clear and `.log` export. See Logs and custom signals for formats and limits.

## About

The About tab shows the installed app version and build number, developer officeyutong, the GitHub profile at https://github.com/officeyutong, offline documentation and bundled open-source licenses. Version information comes from the installed app.

title: Logs and custom signals
summary: Trace formats, APDU and DER modes, and Get EID examples.
body:
# Logs and custom signals

## English raw traces

Logs uses UTC timestamps and records app stages, APDU TX/RX, SW, HTTP method/URL/application-level request and response headers, status codes, body chunks in hexadecimal and transport errors.

- `TX` is an attempt to send; `RX` is a received response. A timeout does not prove that the card did not execute the command.
- `HEX` contains the actual bytes. Reassemble bodies by message ID and `offset`; `length` gives the total byte count.
- `SW=9000` is an APDU success status. The response body must still be parsed to determine the ES10 operation result.
- This is app-visible application signaling, not a capture of all phone traffic, encrypted TLS records or internal baseband QMI messages.
- The in-memory trace retains approximately 4 MiB, then evicts older records and reports their count. Export creates a `.log` file.
- Raw HTTP/APDU data may contain activation credentials, certificates, encrypted profile packages and card identifiers.

## Raw APDU mode

Enter one short APDU per line, up to 64 commands. Use hexadecimal and whitespace; lines beginning with `#` are comments. Length must be 4–261 bytes with consistent Lc and optional Le. Extended-length APDUs are unsupported.

Use a basic-channel CLA such as `00` or `80`. The app binds the allocated logical channel and supports CLA encoding for channels 0–19.

Responses remain raw. There is no automatic `61xx` or `6Cxx` handling. The default stops a batch on a status other than `9000`; turn it off to arrange GET RESPONSE or other commands yourself. Commands are never retried automatically.

Read-only Get EID example; the example button fills text without sending:

```text
80 E2 91 00 06 BF 3E 03 5C 01 5A
```

## ES10 DER mode

Enter one complete DER TLV. The existing libeuicc sends STORE DATA blocks and collects subsequent `61xx` responses. The console shows the concatenated response body; Logs contains every APDU and SW.

- Uses the configured MSS, default 120.
- Limits: 256 request blocks, 4096 exchanges and 1 MiB of responses.
- This mode currently permits channels 0–3 because of the library's channel encoding.
- Arbitrary HTTP requests are not provided.

The DER for the same Get EID request:

```text
BF 3E 03 5C 01 5A
```

## Send and finish

Review the bytes, tap Send and confirm. Requests share the serial operation queue and close the channel afterward. Responses received before an error remain available. Custom commands can modify or erase profiles; reading an article never executes them.

Both read-only Get EID modes passed on the device in 1.2.1. Raw mode returned 6115, then completed with 9000 when the request and GET RESPONSE were sent in one batch with stop-on-status disabled. DER mode automatically collected the identical EID body. No card-modifying custom commands were tested.

title: Technical architecture
summary: Native LPA, local IPC, CommCenter and the card transport.
body:
# Technical architecture

The device-tested baseline is an iPhone 13 (iPhone14,5), iOS 17.2.1 / 21C66, roothide, with the removable eSTK eUICC in slot 2. Version 1.1.4 passed the native Test profile download/rename/enable/disable/restore/delete round trip. Version 1.1.7 passed the final device read-only checks. Version 1.2.1 passed device checks of documents/languages, logs and read-only custom signaling. Version 1.2.2 updates these bundled validation records without changing the transport core.

## Data flow

```text
UIKit interface / native libeuicc LPA
  + ES9+ -> NSURLSession HTTPS -> operator server
  + ES10 -> local HMAC IPC -> native CommCenter extension
                    -> subscriber / QMI driver
                    -> removable eUICC ISD-R
APDU and application-level HTTP exchanges -> English log
```

The app runs the LPA on the phone. The extension provides SIM-slot, logical-channel and APDU transport. Frida is a research/debugging tool, not a runtime requirement. Normal use does not require a computer to relay APDU or HTTP traffic.

Profile management and custom requests share a serial queue so that card reads, downloads and switching cannot concurrently own the management channel.

## Persistent card session

The high-level CommCenter sender accepts an **AID**, not an arbitrary raw APDU. The extension uses it to establish an ISD-R session and intercepts the driver's channel-close path to retain the session. It replaces generated APDU data for subsequent app requests, captures raw responses, then closes the channel and releases the original completion callback when finished.

When the SIM is inactive, the extension opens the management channel through the driver entry point. This allows management reads and line restoration after disabling a profile.

## App–extension communication

The app listens on `127.0.0.1:18099`. Bounded newline-delimited JSON carries requests and matching replies. A random challenge and role-separated HMAC authenticate both peers. The listener is not exposed remotely. This pairing does not isolate jailbreak root privileges; the app and extension are built with the same project pairing key.

The extension derives addresses and fields at runtime with driver-scoped CoreSymbolication, Frida devkit Capstone, RTTI and live-object checks. Both image UUIDs and the private ABI must be approved before hooks or card commands. The Firmware resolver screen exposes evidence; the Porting article explains the rules and remaining manual work.

## Network and logging

NSURLSession implements ES9+ HTTPS with system trust plus the bundled GSMA root and hostname verification. App-specific wireless access can be enabled without changing the trust store.

The log records app-visible APDU and application-level HTTP data. It does not capture encrypted TLS records or all internal modem signaling. The separate Logs and custom signals article describes retention, byte formats and command limits.

title: Porting guide
summary: Firmware UUIDs, private ABI, offsets and validation steps.
body:
# Porting and runtime discovery

## Runtime resolver in 1.3

The extension decodes ARM64 with Capstone 5 from the Frida Gum 17.25.0 devkit. Private symbols are enumerated with CoreSymbolication only in the driver module. Normal use needs no Frida server, JavaScript or computer. Substrate still installs the hooks.

Image analysis discovers 18 code locations/fields; read-only live-object inspection discovers two more fields. Candidates must be unique. Reports preserve evidence and failure state. There is no old numerical-offset fallback. Open Card management > Firmware resolver to refresh or copy the report; the report sends no APDU.

- Mach-O supplies loaded bases, code ranges, UUIDs and LC_FUNCTION_STARTS. Symbol candidates must be function starts inside the target image.
- Driver symbols and block instructions identify open/command/close, encoder, response and QMI callbacks and their captured fields.
- C++ RTTI, vtables and the virtual-method/worker/closure-constructor relationship locate SubscriberSimController, sender, worker and completion.
- Worker instructions identify the SimInfo vector, logical-slot field and state getter. The exported isSimReady predicate replaces a fixed state enum.
- Exported Registry getters supply the service map. A bounded linked-object search matches the unique controller vtable, removing the old map/node/typeinfo/vtable-slot offsets.
- Driver pointers require the exact concrete RTTI name, excluding shared_ptr control blocks whose type names also contain the driver name. Hardware-slot fields are checked across SimInfo nodes; logical and hardware slots remain distinct.

## Example discovery results

These are observations on iPhone14,5 / iOS 17.2.1, not configuration values or portable constants. Addresses are relative to their respective images. See tweak/ResolverCore.cpp, tweak/RuntimeResolver.mm and tweak/Apdu.mm.

| Item | Observed result |
|---|---|
| CommCenter UUID | 10bdb2fd04e33fcea0a188d064801df2 |
| Driver UUID | 571c9998ee7c3d9e946f779aee761332 |
| sender / worker | CommCenter +0x7e4568 / +0x7ff250 |
| Controller vtable / completion | CommCenter +0x175fb78 / +0x803a74 |
| SimInfo state getter | CommCenter +0x11c3c10 |
| SimInfo vector / logical slot | Controller +0xa8 / SimInfo +0x24 |
| Driver open / command / close | Driver +0x168858 / +0x1693e0 / +0x16a7a4 |
| Encoder / QMI / response | Driver +0x169bb8 / +0x16a214 / +0x16a43c |
| Encoder channel / response hardware slot / channel | Block +0x30 / +0x30 / +0x34 |
| QMI error field | Result +0x4 |
| Controller driver pointer / SimInfo hardware slot | Live object +0x68 / +0x20 |
| Ready predicate / Registry | Exported subscriber::isSimReady and Registry::getServiceMap |

## Supporting another build

1. Record the device, baseband, architecture and both image UUIDs. First run a diagnostic-only build and save the report. Unknown UUID pairs can be analyzed but install no hooks and send no card commands.
2. If code discovery succeeds uniquely, verify private signatures, argument order, C++ value/reference passing, block semantics, callback lifetime and PAC. The native build measures shared_ptr as 16 bytes and std::function as 32 bytes. A 48-byte buffer in early Frida research was not sizeof(std::function). Matching sizes alone do not prove ABI compatibility.
3. Add the verified UUID pair and sizes to SHApprovedAbis in shared/Firmware.h. Normally no numerical offsets need entering. When a pattern changes, update its semantic rule and add image replay/negative cases while preserving old-build regression coverage.
4. Verify injection, arm64/arm64e, Substrate and rootless/roothide packaging. Start with live-object inspection, logical/hardware slot mapping, Get EID, listing, 61xx, channel close and disconnect recovery.
5. Then use an authorized, redownloadable profile to test download, enable, disable, restore and delete, comparing the original baseline individually. The default slot 2 does not identify physical slots on other devices.
6. Test wireless policy, GSMA TLS, camera/photos, foreground/background and restart separately. Standard LPA/UI code is usually reusable. Internal eUICC, MEP, other basebands and USB readers require separate transport work.

Discovery reduces address/field maintenance; it cannot establish calling conventions or slot semantics automatically. Only the UUID pair above is approved. Missing cached symbols, stripped RTTI, changed instructions or ambiguous objects reject card operations. Live-object rules currently require 2-16 SimInfo nodes and a unique hardware-slot field with values 1-3. Single-node or different mappings need revised rules and device validation.

## Resource and validation limits

CommCenter has a small memory budget. Early process-wide Gum symbol enumeration caused memory-highwater termination, was rolled back and removed. The final design scopes CoreSymbolication to the driver and explicitly registers Capstone ARM64 and libc allocators without global Gum/GLib caches. maxMeasuredFootprintBytes is the maximum of a few stage samples, not a continuously measured process peak. Expected resolution failures return errors without C++ exception unwinding.

The new resolver still requires write/switch regression. This round's read-only checks cannot replace the 1.1.4 complete write test or establish other-firmware compatibility.

title: Compatibility and validation
summary: Device-tested results, offline checks and unsupported features.
body:
# Compatibility and validation

## Runtime discovery validation in 1.3.4

On iPhone 13 (iPhone14,5), iOS 17.2.1 / 21C66 with roothide, all 18 code locations/fields and two live-object fields resolve uniquely. Native profile/details reads and test notifications pass. The test profiles match the immediate pretest baseline individually; the original test profile remains enabled. No download, enable/disable, deletion or reset was performed.

Linux image replay and a standalone iPhone program pass real-image, ASLR relocation, missing/ambiguous/interior-symbol, unreadable-image and cyclic/ambiguous-object-graph cases. Linux also passes ASan/UBSan. Unknown UUIDs and mismatched object sizes reject private-ABI approval.

Early process-wide Gum enumeration caused memory-highwater termination and was rolled back to 1.2.2. Subsequent fixes explicitly register Capstone ARM64, return initialization failures without exception unwinding and exclude shared_ptr control blocks from concrete-driver RTTI matching. The final design avoids global symbol caches and decodes incrementally to reduce temporary allocations.

This round did not repeat the complete write/switch flow. The previous 1.1.4 write results apply to the earlier transport. The resolver currently approves only the build above; these results do not establish other-iOS compatibility.

## Previous device research

Baseline: iPhone 13 (iPhone14,5), iOS 17.2.1 / 21C66, roothide, removable eSTK card in slot 2.

- 1.1.4 passed the complete test-profile download, rename, enable, disable, original-line restore and delete flow. The final test profiles matched individually.
- 1.1.7 passed card/notification reads, TLS, QR-image decoding and settings/notification UI checks. Camera preview checks passed.
- The original test profile was restored. Cellular data, SMS and calls were not tested.
- An earlier switch test encountered a management-channel issue after disabling a profile. Recovery and a fix followed; original profiles were not deleted.

## Validation for 1.2.x

Version 1.2.0 added English signaling logs, custom APDU/DER and bilingual UI. Version 1.2.1 added this offline manual and passed the device checks below. Version 1.2.2 updates the bundled records without changing the transport core.

- Native card/notification reads, TLS and QR-image decoding passed.
- All five articles opened and copied in both languages. Title/body/offset searches and the no-results state passed.
- English, Simplified Chinese and Follow system applied immediately. Dark-mode documents passed; logs remained English with Chinese UI.
- Raw APDU and ES10 DER Get EID returned identical results. A raw batch completed 61xx -> GET RESPONSE -> 9000.
- APDU/HTTP trace display, copy, matching export contents, share cancellation cleanup and clearing passed.
- Profiles matched the immediate pretest baseline individually. The enabled line and language preference were preserved. This round performed no download, enable/disable, deletion or reset.

Offline checks also cover language resources, manual/example/UUID/offset consistency, codecs, malformed inputs, CLA mapping, ASan/UBSan and real libeuicc mock-card flows for MSS 6/120/255, 256 blocks, 61xx and errors.

These results do not establish compatibility with every device, operator or custom command. Debug-driven interface checks are not acceptance tests of a physical camera scan.

## OpenEUICC feature comparison

Implemented interfaces include listing, downloading, enabling/disabling, renaming, deleting, card information, notification management and automatic-notification settings, default SM-DP+, optional download IMEI, proxy, MSS, switch refresh and confirmation-based entire-card reset.

- Proxy, IMEI, default-server changes, nondefault MSS/refresh and reset have not been fully tested on the current card. Reset has not been executed.
- Android OMAPI/system integration, MEP, multiple readers, USB CCID, forced TPDU, custom ISD-R AID and SM-DS automatic discovery are unsupported.
- There is no option to bypass TLS verification.
- Card policy can reject switching, deletion or reset. A feature's presence does not establish compatibility with every card.

The comparison used the official OpenEUICC repository at `https://gitea.angry.im/PeterCxy/OpenEUICC`, revision `2cbd7a1b3f2482003ace1583b64abf4015283e5a`.

## Remaining coverage

Other devices/firmware, all operators, installation interruption, card removal and prolonged background recovery have not been fully covered. UUID checks prevent applying existing offsets to unmatched firmware. Start the next device checks with read-only Get EID, inspect the trace and channel closure, then consider explicitly authorized writes.
